newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae, group differ on meeting date.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae, group differ on meeting date.

text.p: A group of Student Loan Marketing Association shareholders called the Committee to Restore Value said Thursday it will conduct a special meeting on May 9, and insisted Sallie Mae management does not have the right to set the time of the special meeting sought by the committee.

The Sallie Mae management said in a press release that it has scheduled its own special meeting for 1000 EDT May 15 at the Ritz Carlton Hotel in McLean, Va. Sallie Mae said it has set the time for the Committee's meeting at 1400 EDT on May 15 at the same location.
"It's clear to us that the (Sallie Mae) Chairman (William Arceneaux) has the authority to set both meetings on the same day," a Sallie Mae spokeswoman said.
Albert Lord, a Sallie Mae director and a spokesman for the Committee, said Arceneaux "has assumed a right to call a meeting that he doesn't have. The by-laws of the company are quite clear."
Lord added, "we have kept our original offer to him open, to conduct the meetings simultaneously. He has taken it upon himself to refuse to do that."
The purpose of Sallie Mae's May 15 meeting is to vote on management's plan of reorganizaton that will change Sallie Mae from a government-sponsored enterprise to a private corporation.
Lord is one of eight directors elected in 1995. The group ran on a platform it said was aimed at increasing shareholder value.

In the current dispute the committee backs a privatization plan that like the management plan would restructure Sallie Mae into a private corpororation with publicly traded shares. But the commitee has said other proposals that it backs are more "shareholder friendly."
Sallie Mae has said the current management deserves credit for policies which resulted in a tripling of the share price over a two and a half year-period.
